speaker: therapist
text: Good morning Lakshmi garu, thank you for bringing Ravi today. I will ask some questions while he plays, is that okay?

speaker: parent
text: Yes madam, avunu, that is fine. He already went to the toy corner.

speaker: therapist
text: When you talk to Ravi at home, does he look at you?

speaker: parent
text: No madam, he does not look at us when we talk. Even when I feed him he never looks in my eyes.

speaker: therapist
text: And when you call his name from another room?

speaker: parent
text: He does not turn when we call his name. I call Ravi, Ravi, many times, kani he keeps playing.

speaker: therapist
text: Note: child did not respond to name in three attempts, rate item 5 as 4.

speaker: parent
text: Same thing at home, madam. My mother says he is in his own world.

speaker: therapist
text: Let us talk about speech. Did Ravi ever say words?

speaker: parent
text: Yes, at age 2 he said a few words, amma, nanna, ball. Then slowly he stopped talking. Now he says no words at all.

speaker: therapist
text: Thank you for telling me, that is important. Did anything else happen around that time?

speaker: parent
text: Nothing special. My husband said boys talk late, so we waited. Kani the words did not come back.

speaker: therapist
text: How does he play at home?

speaker: parent
text: He lines up his toys in one long line, cars, blocks, even spoons. He plays alone, he does not play with his cousins.

speaker: therapist
text: Does he keep any one toy with him all the time?

speaker: parent
text: Yes, one small red car. He takes it to bed, to the bathroom, everywhere.

speaker: therapist
text: Does he make other sounds or repeat things he hears?

speaker: parent
text: He repeats lines from cartoons, the same line again and again, but not to talk to us.

speaker: therapist
text: Does he point at things he wants, or to show you something?

speaker: parent
text: No, he does not point. If he wants water he pulls my hand to the kitchen.

speaker: therapist
text: How does he react to noises at home?

speaker: parent
text: He covers his ears at the mixer and the pressure cooker whistle. Sometimes he runs and hides behind the sofa.

speaker: therapist
text: And when he is happy or excited?

speaker: parent
text: He flaps his hands very fast and jumps on his toes, chala fast, when the cartoon song comes.

speaker: therapist
text: Note: child flapped hands twice during play today, rate item 24 as 4.

speaker: parent
text: Yes, just now also he did it with the red car.

speaker: therapist
text: What happens when something changes in his routine?

speaker: parent
text: Big tantrum. One day we changed the route to school because of traffic. He screamed and kicked for half an hour.

speaker: therapist
text: When he is upset like that, does he ever hurt himself?

speaker: parent
text: Yes madam, this worries me most. He hits his own head with his hand when he is upset. I hold his hands so he is safe.

speaker: therapist
text: Thank you, that helps me. Does he come to tell you about his day?

speaker: parent
text: No, he never comes to tell us anything. He only takes my hand when he needs something.

speaker: therapist
text: How are his sleep and food?

speaker: parent
text: Sleep is okay but late. He eats only rice and curd from the same plate every day.

speaker: therapist
text: Thank you Lakshmi garu. I only document what I see and what you share, and we will plan the next steps together.

speaker: parent
text: Thank you madam, chala thanks. I just want to help him.
